body:
Greptile Summary

 The PR adds a bounded in-memory cache for fully walked, chunkless directory listings and invalidates those listings alongside local metadata mutations. - Adds paginated listing construction, cached serving with TTL filtering, and LRU eviction. - Adds the `-dirListCacheEntries` mount option and propagates it into the metadata cache. - Adds coverage for cache hits, mutation invalidation, partial walks, expiry, eviction, and disabling the cache.

Confidence Score: 4/5

 The PR does not appear safe to merge until concurrent directory walks can no longer mutate and publish the same listing build without synchronization. Concurrent continuations at the same cursor still receive one shared listing build, append to its slice while holding only a shared read lock, and can publish that raced slice for later directory reads. **Files Needing Attention:** weed/mount/meta_cache/meta_cache.go, weed/mount/meta_cache/listing_cache.go

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | weed/mount/meta_cache/listing_cache.go | Introduces listing build tracking, publication, invalidation, and entry-budget-based eviction. | | weed/mount/meta_cache/meta_cache.go | Integrates cached listing construction and serving into metadata-cache reads and routes store mutations through invalidating wrappers. | | weed/command/mount.go | Adds the configurable directory-listing cache capacity flag. | | weed/command/mount_common.go | Propagates the configured listing-cache capacity into the mount filesystem options. | | weed/mount/meta_cache/listing_cache_test.go | Covers the principal sequential cache lifecycle, pagination, expiry, invalidation, eviction, and disabled-mode behavior. |

body:
Raised `-dirListCacheEntries` to 1,000,000.

Measured what one entry actually retains before picking the number, since the
flag is only useful if an operator can reason about it: a chunkless child holds
about **480 bytes**, so 200k was ~91 MiB and the new default bounds the cache
near **450 MiB**.

The reason a number that large is still reasonable is that it is a ceiling, not
a reservation — nothing is held for a directory that was never walked, so a
mount over ordinary directories never approaches it, and a mount that does walk
a million cached children is exactly the one that wants the speedup. Both the
constant's doc and the flag help now say what reaching it costs, so anyone on a
memory-tight host has the number to lower it against rather than discovering it.

Worth noting for anyone sizing this: a directory larger than the whole budget is
never cached at all, so raising the ceiling is also what lets a single very wide
directory be cached rather than skipped.

Closing in favor of #10634: the kernel serves warm listings from the directory's page cache at a fraction of the code, with memory the kernel reclaims under pressure, and it also covers the read-through directories of #10631 which a mount-side cache never sees. The branch stays around for what the kernel cannot do — consumers with no kernel above the WFS layer, and serving lookup storms from a decoded listing — if either ever becomes pressing.
